title: Short Stuff: Unique Snowflakes
summary: Short Stuff episode on whether snowflakes are unique. The hosts explain that snowflakes begin as small hexagonal ice plates formed when water vapor condenses and freezes around a nucleus like a dust particle, then grow through deposition as vapor freezes onto arms. Temperature and humidity shape the crystal (colder and more humid yields more intricate, fern-like flakes; drier air yields flatter ones). Collisions, broken arms, and local variations in air make each flake's path unique. They cite an estimate of combinations exceeding the number of atoms in the universe and conclude that no two snowflakes are alike. They close with contact information for the show.

segments.title: Opening banter on snowflakes being unique
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the short episode on the saying that every snowflake is unique and joke about the term snowflake.

segments.title: How snowflakes start: water vapor and the template
segments.summary: Water evaporates, rises as vapor, and condenses around dust or a nucleus, then freezes into a small six-sided hexagonal plate, the template all snowflakes start from.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the discussion of later formation.

segments.title: Deposition and growing arms
segments.summary: Water vapor goes straight to ice through deposition and attaches to the plate, forming arms and detailed structure layer by layer.

segments.title: Temperature and humidity shape snowflakes
segments.summary: Jagged edges attract more vapor and build intricate fern-like arms. Colder temperatures and higher humidity produce the most detailed flakes, while lower humidity yields flatter flakes and higher humidity fatter ones.

segments.title: Variables and the odds of two identical snowflakes
segments.summary: Collisions, broken arms, and differing air conditions at each small location add variables. Hosts cite an estimate of combinations exceeding the number of atoms in the universe and argue identical snowflakes are effectively impossible.

segments.title: Closing and contact information
segments.summary: Hosts summarize that no two snowflakes are alike and give the website and email for listener contact.
